# Motivation
In many scenarios, we may be interested in simulating survival times from a population based on the corresponding life tables. For instance, in relative survival analysis [@rubio:2019] [@eletti:2022] [@basak:2025] simulation studies require the simulation of times to event based on life tables. These life tables are stratified on certain characteristics such as age, year, and deprivation level. The life table defines a piecewise-constant rate hazard function, for each combination of characteristics, which can be used to simulate the times to event.

The [SimLT](https://github.com/FJRubio67/SimLT) R package allows for simulating times to event, based on the information in a life table. 

The following R code presents a step-by-step illustrative example om the simulation of times to event based on life tables from England for the years 2010-2015. The `SimLT` R package requires functions from the R packages [msm](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/msm/index.html) and [lubridate](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/lubridate/index.html), which I decided not to include as dependencies. Thus, the user needs to install them and load them manually.

See also: [GHSurv](https://github.com/FJRubio67/GHSurv), [LBANS](https://github.com/FJRubio67/LBANS) [HazReg](https://github.com/FJRubio67/HazReg)

# Illustrative example: R code
In this example we will simulate $n=1000$ times to event using a life table from England based on year, sex, deprivation level, age, English region (gor). The life table can be downloaded from [SimLT](https://github.com/FJRubio67/SimLT).

## Data preparation
```{r}
rm(list=ls())

# Required packages
#library(devtools)
#install_github("FJRubio67/SimLT")
library(SimLT)
library(msm)
library(lubridate)

#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Life tables
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
LT <- as.data.frame(read.table("England_LT_2010_2015_dep_gor.txt",header = T))
head(LT)
```

## Simulated design matrix
We now simulate the individuals' characteristics using the built-in function `simDesMatrix`. These characteristics will be used to simulate the times to event. This function is based on real data on colon and lung (male and female) patients in England. You can use your own design matrix instead.

```{r}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Design matrix simulation 
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sample size
n <- 1000
# Design matrix
Xcf <- simDesMatrix(seed = 123, n = n, admin.cens = "31-12-2015", scale.age = FALSE,
                    site = "colon", sex = "female")
head(Xcf)
```

## Follow-up period
Define the follow-up period. This requires commands from the R package `lubridate`.
```{r}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Follow-up period
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# fixed points (new year and last day of follow-up)
year.init <- 2010
last.day <- as.Date("2015-12-31")
fixed.times <- c(seq(as.Date("2010-01-01"), as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "year"),last.day)
```

## Time points and hazard rates
Now, we need to define the time points that define the step function associated to the piecewise-constant rate hazard function.

```{r}
#------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Time points and hazard rates
#------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Date of diagnosis and date of birth (29 February is moved to 1 March)
dod <- as.Date(Xcf$date.diag)
dob <- as.POSIXlt(dod - Xcf$age*365.25)
leap <- dob$mday == 29 & dob$mon == 1
dob$mday[leap] <- 1
dob$mon[leap] <- 2
dob <- as.Date(format(dob, "%Y-%m-%d"))

# sex
sex0 <- 2

# Candidate time points for all patients at once:
# date of diagnosis, new years, birthdays, and last day of follow-up
yrs <- year.init:year(last.day)
cand <- data.frame(
  id   = c(1:n, rep(1:n, each = length(yrs)), rep(1:n, each = length(yrs)), 1:n),
  date = c(dod,
           rep(as.Date(paste0(yrs, "-01-01")), n),
           as.Date(paste0(rep(yrs, n), rep(format(dob, "-%m-%d"), each = length(yrs)))),
           rep(last.day, n)))
# Keep the points between diagnosis and the last day of follow-up, sorted by patient and date
cand <- cand[cand$date >= dod[cand$id] & cand$date <= last.day, ]
cand <- unique(cand)
cand <- cand[order(cand$id, cand$date), ]

# Age (completed years) at each time point
cand$age <- year(cand$date) - year(dob[cand$id]) -
  (format(cand$date, "%m%d") < format(dob[cand$id], "%m%d"))

# Extracting the hazard rates from the life table for each patient at "age + t":
# a single hashed lookup on (year, sex, dep, age, gor) for all patients
LT.key <- paste(LT$X_year, LT$sex, LT$dep, LT$age, LT$gor)
key <- paste(year(cand$date), sex0, Xcf$dep[cand$id], cand$age, Xcf$gor[cand$id])
cand$rate <- LT$rate[match(key, LT.key)]

# Dates, lengths of times in days between time points, and hazard rates for each patient
dates  <- unname(split(cand$date, cand$id))
times  <- lapply(dates, function(d) c(0, as.numeric(diff(d))))
hrates <- unname(split(cand$rate, cand$id))

# List containing the time points, hazard rates, and dates
Xcf_rates <- list(times = times, hrates = hrates, dates = dates)

```



## Simulating the times to event
Now, we simulate the times to event using the command `sim_pophaz`. This requires a seed for the simulation, and a list with time points at which the piecewise hazard jumps (times) and the values of the piecewise hazard (hrates). This list was constructed in the previous subsection.  

```{r}
##################################################################################################
# Population survival times
##################################################################################################
simC <- sim_pophaz(seed = 123,lst = Xcf_rates, method = "direct")
sim.pop <- simC$sim.pop
status.pop <- simC$status

# Censoring
table(status.pop)


library(survival)

# Kaplan-Meier estimator for the simulated times
kmsim <- survfit(Surv(sim.pop, status.pop) ~ 1)

# Comparison
plot(kmsim$time, kmsim$surv, type = "l", col = "black", lwd = 2, lty = 1, ylim = c(0,1),
     xlab = "Time", ylab = "Survival", cex.axis = 1.5, cex.lab = 1.5, main = "")

```
